item.description:

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: NASA.
Summary: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.
